findings.title: Health Care's 86% earnings bet
findings.body: Health Care's forward multiple sits at the same percentile as its trailing one, yet the forward P/E is 46 percent lower. That compression implies analysts expect 86 percent earnings growth, a bet that looks aggressive for a sector whose valuation has not moved.

findings.title: Materials' extreme lens divergence
findings.body: Materials' trailing P/E sits at the 94th percentile while its forward multiple is at the 42nd, a 53-point gap. The market is pricing in 128 percent earnings growth, which would be a dramatic turnaround from the reported earnings that currently look so expensive.

findings.title: Utilities' month-long valuation collapse
findings.body: Utilities' forward percentile dropped 32 points in one month, landing at the 23rd percentile, while its trailing percentile sits at just 8. The sector has become cheap on both lenses, but the forward multiple still implies 12 percent earnings growth, suggesting the selloff reflects more than just earnings expectations.
